about: What real machines, and the people using them, showed must change in Windstorm Tardigrade, and the version each change is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_tardigrade.py (class Promises) refuses a version while a row due in it is not built, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist and be named in the plan next to the codon.
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person the skill is for, on his own machine: its date moves only by his word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, an ungraceful restart of a Mac test machine on 0.1.7: the note went into two sessions on a login at its weekly limit; Claude Code answered that the limit was hit and held the note, to run by itself as a turn at the reset, about 9 hours later, with nobody there. rows.promise: The wake-up note is never typed into a session whose conversation last ended on a usage or limit reply; the log names it, and the README says a typed note can wait in Claude Code's queue for a reset. After each note the screen is looked at once more, and a note held for the reset is named in the log and in the counts. A limit belongs to the login: once a note typed in this run meets it (limit words new on that screen after the note; an old limit reply in a conversation, or on a resumed screen, holds that session's note only), no other session on the same login gets a note in that run, so sessions sharing one login do not all run stale notes at once at the reset. A wake_text whose words read as a limit notice is refused, by setup and by every run, which types the default note instead. NOT covered: the first session on a login at its limit that has not yet met it in its own conversation still gets the note; Tardigrade then only says it is waiting, and never presses Esc for the person.

Wrong since 0.1.8: each boot start replaces its waiting screen through tmux respawn-pane (a retry has since 0.1.0), and tmux 3.4 gives that pane the PATH of the client that asks, which was the boot service's, with no ~/.local/bin. No machine of ours showed it: each had that folder another way (in the service manager's PATH, claude in /usr/bin, or a shell startup file adding it).
rows.promise: a session started at boot gets the same clean environment whether its pane is new or a waiting screen being replaced, so the program is found wherever its own installer put it: through the path setting exactly as written, or, with none, the default (a standard PATH plus ~/.local/bin) first and then every whole folder of the boot service's own PATH that the default lacks, once each, so a pane never has less than before.

declined.heard: 2026-11-21, the first real reboot of a shared machine with 98 sessions, as seen by the agent that runs that machine: two services of one of the machine's users both carried the same network tunnel, and the second looped on a failure to bind its port.
declined.why: Two services fighting over one thing is the machine's own configuration. Tardigrade will list a user's units that a reboot changes (G3.11); it does not judge whether two of them conflict.
